//: The interactive half. Builds the repo's one ../Dockerfile, same as docker/compose.yaml, so the two front ends cannot drift into different toolchains. HOST_UID/HOST_GID default to 1000 here because devcontainer.json cannot run `id -u`; on a host where you are not uid 1000, either edit these two values or use devtools/devcontainer.sh, which passes the real ones.
name: rustflow
//mounts: The three volumes are mounted by the same names docker/compose.yaml declares, so both front ends warm one cargo registry, one /target and one Claude Code login rather than a cold copy each. rustflow-claude-config is CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR in the Dockerfile; it is what makes a login outlast a container recreate. The fourth entry hands the host's ~/.claude.json to postCreateCommand below, READ-ONLY and under a different name: that file is one monolithic JSON rewritten whole on every change, so the container takes its own copy rather than sharing it. NOTE: unlike devtools/devcontainer.sh, which can test for the file first, docker refuses to start a container whose bind source is missing -- so on a host that has never run Claude Code, drop this line.
//containerEnv: All three are optional and forwarded from the host, matching the `environment:` list in docker/compose.yaml. ${localEnv:VAR} expands to the empty string when the host has no such variable; an empty value is not a configured credential, so a machine that sets neither of Claude Code's two still gets the interactive /login path.
//postCreateCommand: The same script devtools/devcontainer.sh runs after its own `up`, so the two front ends cannot drift: it sets up git push credentials from GH_TOKEN and seeds Claude Code's config from the mount above. Per-created-container, which is right -- both of those land in the container's own filesystem.
